record.title: Two-trait crosses and independent assortment — video support
record.purpose: List valid gametes for two loci, use a Punnett square or product rule, and identify the assumption of independent assortment.
record.fallback: For AaBb × AaBb, the A locus gives a 3/4 dominant-phenotype probability and 1/4 recessive probability. The B locus gives the same. If the loci assort independently, the probability of both dominant phenotypes is 3/4 × 3/4 = 9/16. The other phenotype combinations are 3/16, 3/16 and 1/16, producing the familiar 9:3:3:1 expectation. This ratio is specific to the stated heterozygote cross and allele relationships. For a different cross, recompute. In AaBb × aaBb, probability of A_ is 1/2 and probability of B_ is 3/4, so both dominant phenotypes have probability 3/8. A memorized 9/16 would be wrong.

exactNearestTeachingParagraphs.exactHtml: Before meiosis, DNA is copied. Each chromosome then consists of two sister chromatids, the copied versions joined together. Copying an R-bearing chromosome produces two R-bearing sister copies; it does not turn r into R or mix the two allele versions. We are following ordinary copying and separation, without a mutation changing the allele.

Meiosis reduces the chromosome sets from two to one. The homologous chromosomes separate in the first division. The sister chromatids separate in the second division, with no further DNA copying between those divisions. A cell with one chromosome set is haploid. In a flowering plant, the reproductive life cycle produces haploid gametes after this reduction. We only need to follow the allele contribution here: an egg or sperm carries one allele at this locus, not the parent's whole pair.

Check your response: keep the first parent's list; reduce the second to Rt; size the grid from those lists; show the two tt outcomes; explain why the colour conclusion survives while the height probability changes. A four-by-two grid would add an unnecessary duplicate column if both columns represented Rt. It would not create another gamete type. Retaining the old RT column would be a different error: RRtt cannot contribute T.

For specified independent events, multiply probabilities. Two recessive offspring in a row from Aa × Aa have probability 1/4 × 1/4 = 1/16. Do not confuse this ordered event with “at least one recessive among two,” which asks for a different set of outcomes.
